title: Bowling Game with Time Control
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a 3D bowling game featuring time control (slow-motion and fast-forward) using Three.js.

## Scene Setup
- Use Three.js with OrbitControls and GLTFLoader from CDN.
- Create a bowling lane: a long rectangular box (width: 3, height: 0.2, length: 20) with brown/wood color, centered at (0, -0.1, 0), extending from z=-10 to z=10.
- Place 10 bowling pins arranged in standard triangle formation at z=-8. Each pin is a white cylinder (radius 0.15, height 0.6) placed on the lane surface (y=0.3). Pin positions in rows: Row1(1 pin at z=-8), Row2(2 pins at z=-8.6), Row3(3 pins at z=-8.2*2=-9.2), Row4(4 pins at z=-9.8). Space pins 0.5 apart in x. Store pins in an array.
- Load the 'AntiqueCamera.glb' model using GLTFLoader. Scale it to 0.5 and position it at (4, 1, 5) beside the lane as a decorative "replay camera" prop. Add a small label div overlay saying "Replay Cam".
- Create a bowling ball: a sphere (radius 0.3) with dark blue MeshStandardMaterial, initially at position (0, 0.3, 8).
- Camera at (0, 5, 12) looking at (0, 0, 0). Add DirectionalLight at (5, 10, 5) and AmbientLight.
- Add wooden gutter zones on each side of the lane (x < -1.5 or x > 1.5).

## Physics (Simple Custom Physics)
- Implement simple physics: the ball moves forward (negative z) when launched. Ball velocity stored as {x, y, z}.
- Pin collision: when ball center is within 0.5 units of a pin base, that pin is "knocked down" — rotate it 90 degrees on x-axis and mark it as fallen.
- Gutter detection: if ball x position goes beyond ±1.5, the ball falls into the gutter (set y to -0.5, stop forward motion).
- Ball stops when z < -10 or velocity magnitude < 0.01.

## Time Control System
- Implement a timeScale variable (default 1.0) that multiplies all physics delta-time.
- Slow-motion button (id='btn-slowmo'): sets timeScale to 0.25
- Normal speed button (id='btn-normal'): sets timeScale to 1.0
- Fast-forward button (id='btn-fastfwd'): sets timeScale to 3.0
- Pause button (id='btn-pause'): sets timeScale to 0.0
- Display current timeScale in a HUD element (id='hud-timescale').

## User Interactions
- Aiming: Left/Right arrow keys adjust ball's initial x-velocity (aim direction). Show aim angle in HUD (id='hud-aim'). Aim value ranges from -2 to 2, step 0.2 per keypress.
- Power: Up/Down arrow keys adjust launch power from 1 to 10 (step 1). Show in HUD (id='hud-power'). Default power: 5.
- Launch: Press Spacebar to launch the ball. Ball gets velocity {x: aimValue * 0.5, y: 0, z: -power * 0.8}.
- Reset: Button (id='btn-reset') resets ball position, re-stands all pins, resets score for current frame.

## Scoring
- Each knocked pin = 1 point. Display score in HUD (id='hud-score').
- Display pins remaining in (id='hud-pins-remaining').
- Track game phase: 'aiming', 'rolling', 'finished'. Display in (id='hud-phase').
- Ball is 'rolling' after launch, 'finished' when ball stops or exits lane.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- ballPosition: {x, y, z} — current ball position
- ballVelocity: {x, y, z} — current ball velocity
- ballLaunched: boolean
- pinsKnocked: number (count of fallen pins)
- pinsRemaining: number (10 - pinsKnocked)
- score: number
- timeScale: number
- aimValue: number
- power: number
- phase: string ('aiming'|'rolling'|'finished')
- gutterBall: boolean
- modelLoaded: boolean (true when AntiqueCamera.glb loads)
- pinStates: array of 10 booleans (true=standing, false=fallen)

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Ball moves with velocity * deltaTime * timeScale. Pin knocked when distance < 0.5. Gutter when |ball.x| > 1.5. Ball stops when z < -10 or speed < 0.01. TimeScale multiplies all physics updates. Power range [1,10], aim range [-2,2].
